findings.title: Working-hours check uses identical start and end values
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, `start` and `end` are both computed as `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` should use the slot end time. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends past them is therefore never rejected. The check is also in UTC minutes and ignores the organizer timezone, so it can wrongly reject valid slots for hosts whose working hours cross midnight in UTC. Slots can be wrongly dropped or wrongly accepted.

findings.title: Dead comparison between Dayjs objects
findings.body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object references, so it is always false. The zero-length override case (a day fully blocked) is never handled by this branch. Use `.isSame()`.

findings.title: Date override matching and offset are fragile
findings.body: The offset is computed with `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)`, which reinterprets the Date as a local time in that zone rather than converting an instant. The sign handling is therefore likely wrong, and DST may be applied incorrectly. The override day is then compared by UTC date string against the slot's UTC date. For invitee timezones far from the organizer, or slots near midnight UTC, the override can be matched to the wrong day, or an override that spans UTC midnight is partly ignored. Only the +5:30 and +6:00 zones are tested.

findings.title: Override offset can wrap across midnight and breaks the day filter
findings.body: The override start and end are shifted by the offset and reduced to hour*60+minute. If the shift crosses midnight, endTime becomes smaller than startTime, or the override moves to the neighbouring day. The result is that the override produces no slots (start >= end is skipped). `activeOverrides` is still filtered using the unshifted UTC start. Also `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through a locale string and loses milliseconds and timezone information; use `dayjs(override.start)`.

findings.title: Timezone test does not verify the behaviour it claims to
findings.body: The new test passes a different invitee timezone but expects identical UTC slots, so it would pass even if timezone handling were broken. The fixed-host date override fix for round robin has no test at all.
